{"method": "cycle_average_fcff", "first_fiscal_year": 2016, "last_fiscal_year": 2024, "trough_year": 2023, "peak_year": 2018, "exclusions": [{"item": "FY2024 patent cross-license agreement gain (one-off item inside the last window year)", "evidence_id": "mu-20250529", "quote": "Patent cross-license agreement gain | — | — | — | 200"}, {"item": "FY2024 benefit from selling inventory written down in a prior year, and the FY2023 write-down that created it", "evidence_id": "mu-20250529", "quote": "Lower costs from sale of inventory written down in prior periods | — | — | — | 987"}, {"item": "FY2023 inventory net-realisable-value write-down charge", "evidence_id": "mu-20250529", "quote": "For example, in 2023, we recorded aggregate charges of $1.83 billion to write down the carrying value of our inventories to their estimated net realizable value."}], "what_would_change_it": "If the annual history gained a completed FY2025 line showing positive FCFF at the guided ~$14 billion net capital-expenditure level, I would shorten the window to the most recent peak-to-peak span (FY2019–FY2025) on the grounds that the FY2016–FY2018 cycle was run at a materially smaller revenue base and lower capital intensity.", "why": "FACT [1] (mu-20250529, annual history, metric `fcff`): FY2018 fcff = 8,660,984,063 USD and FY2023 fcff = -6,325,000,000 USD. FACT [2] (mu-20250529, annual history, metric `fcff`): FY2016 fcff = -2,403,000,000 USD, FY2017 = 3,791,814,087 USD, FY2019 = 3,281,414,301 USD, FY2020 = -69,209,856 USD, FY2021 = 2,231,404,310 USD, FY2022 = 2,771,464,528 USD, FY2024 = -354,404,839 USD. INFERENCE [3, from 1+2]: over the nine usable years the free-cash-flow line swings from roughly minus six billion to plus nine billion dollars and changes sign five times, so no single year in the history is a defensible standing level. FACT [4] (mu-20250529): "In the past five years, annual percentage changes in DRAM average selling prices have ranged from plus low-teen percentage range to a minus high-40% range. In the past five years, annual percentage changes in NAND average selling prices have ranged from plus low-30% to a minus low-50% range." INFERENCE [5, from 3+4]: the swing is priced-driven rather than one-off, which is the condition under which an averaged window rather than a spot year is the right object to capitalise.

Window. FACT [6] (mu-20250529, annual history, `status` column): FY2008 through FY2015 are all marked UNAVAILABLE (e.g. "UNAVAILABLE: missing revenue: absent for the fiscal year ending 2015-09-03"), and FY2016 is the first year with status "ok". INFERENCE [7, from 6]: FY2016 is the earliest permissible start; the window is bounded below by the data, not chosen. INFERENCE [8, from 1+2]: FY2016–FY2024 contains two troughs (FY2016 and the deeper FY2023) and the FY2018 peak, so it spans peak and trough as required; the alternative FY2019–FY2024 window contains the FY2023 trough but its best year (FY2019, 3,281,414,301 USD) is well below FY2018 and would be a trough-weighted window rather than a cycle.

Why not reported_ttm. FACT [9] (mu-20250529, annual history): the latest fiscal year present, FY2024, has fcff = -354,404,839 USD. FACT [10] (mu-20250529, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows): the only FY2025 cash-flow data in the bundle is nine-month — "Net cash provided by operating activities | 11,795 | 5,102" and "Expenditures for property, plant, and equipment | (10,199) | (5,266)" for the nine months ended May 29, 2025. DATA GAP: no annual or trailing-twelve-month FY2025 FCFF exists in the annual history, and converting the nine-month figures into one is not permitted. INFERENCE [11, from 9+10]: reported_ttm would either capitalise a negative FY2024 number or require a restatement I cannot make.

Why not the margin method. FACT [12] (mu-20250529): "Total revenue for the first nine months of 2025 increased 50% as compared to the first nine months of 2024 due to increases in both DRAM and NAND sales. Sales of DRAM products increased 60% primarily due to a high-40% range increase in average selling prices and a high-single-digit percent range increase in bit shipments." INFERENCE [13, from 4+12]: trailing revenue is itself an up-cycle quantity here because it is largely an ASP outcome, so multiplying a cycle-average margin by it would apply a mid-cycle margin to a high-cycle top line and re-import the cyclicality the averaging was meant to remove.

The cost of this choice, stated plainly. FACT [14] (mu-20250529, annual history, `revenue`): FY2016 revenue 12,399,000,000 USD versus FY2024 revenue 25,111,000,000 USD. FACT [15] (mu-20250529): "We estimate capital expenditures in 2025 for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $14 billion." INFERENCE [16, from 14+15]: a dollar average anchored partly in years when the business was half its current revenue understates the scale of the asset now generating cash, while the guided capital-expenditure level is above any single-year FCFF in the history — the two errors point in opposite directions and I cannot size either from the bundle, which is the main weakness of this answer. FACT [17] (mu-20250529): "Following the May 2023 decision of its cybersecurity review of our products sold in China, the CAC determined that critical information infrastructure operators in China may not purchase Micron products". ASSUMPTION: I am treating the FY2016–FY2024 span as one complete industry cycle rather than a period containing a structural break in end-demand; the bundle describes an AI-driven mix shift ("approximately one-half of our total revenue was concentrated in the data center end market") but contains no completed fiscal year in which that mix produced a measured full-year FCFF, so the assumption is untested and a reader who rejects it should reject this window."}
